pm_structure.summary: General account is 100% externally managed (AM Best, Oct 2025); Foresters exited asset management in 2019 (Canadian arm to Fiera Capital, US arm to Macquarie) and retains a small internal Investments team that sets policy and oversees external managers under Board-approved Investment Policy.
manager_entities: External asset managers (not named in FY2025 statements)
Fiera Capital (acquired Foresters Asset Management Aug 2019; expected to keep managing a portion of Foresters assets at the time)
bullets: Board Risk and Investment Committee approves Investment Policy; enterprise-wide and segment-level portfolio limits
Assets segmented by liability block and geography (US branch, Canada, FLIC, UK); managed in relation to each segment's liabilities
Internal Investments team surveys external asset managers annually on ESG; discusses climate/credit risk with managers
FLIC is charged by IOF for shared services incl. investment management (C$8.8mm total support-function charge in 2025)
Asset management sold 2019: FAM (C$10.5bn AUM) to Fiera; US First Investors funds to Macquarie; broker-dealer to Cetera

rotation_commentary.text: Mortgages grew to C$294mm from C$244mm; corporates rose to C$4.68bn from C$4.25bn while governments fell to C$1.54bn from C$1.79bn (AAA bucket halved to C$548mm).
FLIC LPs (real estate, private debt, infrastructure equity) steady at C$46mm; IOF 'other invested assets' (LPs) C$299mm, ~3.7% of invested assets.
Strategy refocused on life insurance; developing a US multi-year guaranteed annuity (MYGA) to diversify an almost all-life product mix (AM Best).
AM Best: ~77% of consolidated invested assets in bonds, <5% below investment grade; some duration mismatch with long-dated liabilities (assets shorter).

debt_outstanding.note: 2.885% to Oct 15 2030 call, then 3M CDOR/alternative + 1.77%; matures Oct 15 2035; carrying value C$248.8mm; interest C$7.4mm/yr
US$100mm facility, undrawn at YE2024; counted in FLIC/IOF liquidity ratio

No CLO, fund-finance, FHLB or sidecar exposure disclosed

deals.text: Acquired Canada Protection Plan Inc. (Oct 1, 2020), its long-standing no-medical distribution partner; now the main Canadian channel
Sold Foresters Life Insurance and Annuity Company (FLIAC, US) to Nassau Group (closed Jul 1, 2020), cutting interest-sensitive/variable exposure
Acquired the Halifax Child Trust Fund block in the UK (plans transferred Apr 2020)
Sold Foresters Asset Management (Canada, ~C$10.5bn AUM) to Fiera Capital; US asset management (First Investors) to Macquarie; broker-dealer to Cetera
Intra-group 100% quota-share coinsurance of FLIC non-par block to IOF (Oct 1, 2021) to optimise capital

sponsorships.text: C$12.1mm invested in member benefits and community giving; 520 scholarships worth C$1.4mm; member grants used by 7,200+ members
Multi-year partnerships with KABOOM! (playgrounds, 20 years) and Whole Kids Foundation (US$45k to 14 organisations, extended to Canada/UK)

bank_relationships.text: US$100mm bank line of credit (undrawn YE2024); lender not named
FX forward counterparties under ISDA/CSA (not named)

appetite: Board-approved Risk Appetite Framework; financial appetite measures defined vs capital, liquidity, credit; market-risk limits set via FCT/ORSA
Investment Policy: investment-grade only for fixed income, single-name and sector concentration limits, segment-specific guidelines
Liquidity: strategic liquidity ratio target 200% under single stress scenario (S&P liquidity model); FLIC ratio shown each year
governance: Board Risk and Investment Committee (RIC) oversees ERM Committee and Global CRO; segment CROs report to Global CRO (Caroline Rendall)
Three lines: business units own risk; Risk Management function reports to ERMC monthly and RIC quarterly; Global Internal Audit (SVP Pat Colavita)
Capital Management Policy sets internal targets at consolidated and segment level; 5-year capital projections; quarterly monitoring; annual FCT
risk.capital_target: Internal LICAT targets above OSFI supervisory levels (100% Total / 70% Core) at consolidated and segment level; values not disclosed. Actual: IOF 188.2% Total / 139.3% Core; FLIC 207.9% / 171.3%; US RBC 623%
sensitivities: IOF rates +100bp: net income/surplus -C$79.1mm (liabilities +328.1, financial instruments -407.2); -100bp: +C$60.2mm
IOF real estate cap rates +/-: C$-0.8mm/+1.2mm (LP real estate)
IOF lapse 10% adverse: -C$117.7mm TCI net of reinsurance; mortality +1%: -C$17.0mm net
FLIC rates +/-1%: FVTPL assets -/+C$8mm; mortality +1%: -C$1.7mm net; lapse 10% adverse: -C$7.6mm net
hedging: FX forward programme (since 2017) to insulate LICAT from USD/CAD moves; notional C$968.8mm at YE2025
No seg-fund dynamic hedge (UK unit-linked guarantees immaterial: C$1k liability)
Mortgage and bond FVTPL designations used to hedge GMM liability interest sensitivity (accounting mismatch reduction)
events: FY2024 IOF net loss C$56.8mm (insurance service loss C$190mm) reversed to C$223.9mm profit in 2025 on investment returns and favourable experience
CEO transition: Louis Gagnon stepped down Jul 2023; Rene Zanin interim; Matt Berman appointed Jan 2024
CPP (CA CPP A-Z permanent/term) lapse assumptions increased in early durations in 2025 assumption review

notes: Two legal entities matter for the deck: FLIC (OSFI id 28432; C$1.8bn assets, LICAT 208%) is small because its non-par block is 100% coinsured to the parent IOF, which carries the group balance sheet (C$19.6bn assets incl. C$10.2bn UK unit-linked; C$8.1bn general-account investments; LICAT 188%). ~98% of insurance revenue is North American; most sales are US. Investment construct is fully outsourced after the 2019 sale of the in-house managers; FX forwards (C$0.97bn) hedge the LICAT ratio.
